title: Exploratory Study of Process-Related Support Needs in Care Counseling in the Context of Digital and AI-Supported Applications
summary:
This study examines how care counselling for people in need of care and their relatives works in practice in Germany and where counsellors need more support.

Care counselling is often complex and time-consuming. At the same time, digital tools and artificial intelligence could help counsellors in their daily work. However, little is known about how these tools can be used in practice and what is actually helpful.

The study therefore talks to care counsellors, experts and, if possible, people who receive counselling. In addition, digital tools are explored in practice to understand how they are used and perceived.

The aim is to identify where support is needed and how digital tools could improve counselling in a meaningful and practical way.
conditions: This study does not focus on a specific disease or diagnosis. Instead, it examines care counselling as a service within the German health and social care system for people in need of care and their relatives. The focus is on counselling processes, organisational conditions and support needs, particularly in relation to digital and AI-supported applications.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Target group Care advisors:
• Employment in a care advisory organization or institution in Germany within the last five years
• Active participation in advisory processes (e.g., initial consultation, care planning, coordination, follow-up) or in the organizational design of these processes
• Minimum age of 18 years
• Willingness to participate voluntarily and to provide informed consent

Target group Experts:
• Professional activity related to care consultation / care infrastructure
• Responsibility for decision-making, management, or implementation

Target group people seeking advice:
• Use of care counseling services (e.g., at care support centers or similar advisory services) 
• Minimum age of 18 years 
• Capacity to give informed consent 
• Voluntary participation regardless of ongoing counseling or benefit decisions
Exclusion criteria:
Target group Care advisors:
• Exclusively administrative or purely technical tasks without any connection to advisory or support processes
• Insufficient German language skills to participate in interviews or group discussions
• Relationships of dependency where voluntary participation does not appear to be guaranteed

Target group Experts:
• no operational or strategic proximity to the field of study

Target group people seeking advice
• Acute crisis situations or psychological stress where participation in the study could represent an additional burden
• Impaired capacity to consent
• Insufficient language skills that prevent informed consent or participation
